Messages.Author: Luis P. Duarte
Messages.Body:
Hi!

- Situation 1:

A sucessfully plays "Blessing of Chaos" on him.
B plays "Bum's Rush" on C.
A blocks and intercepts B action.

Can B play "Thoughts Betrayed"?

- Situation 2:

A enters combat with B.
A plays "Burning Wrath" as strike.
B plays "Entombment" at superior, as strike.

Since A is going to torpor, does B still takes the damage, (and
goes to torpor too) ?

Thanx!
.- Luis....@ip.pt (aka The Gothlord)

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
Luis P. Duarte wrote:
>
> Hi!
>
> - Situation 1:
>
> A sucessfully plays "Blessing of Chaos" on him.
> B plays "Bum's Rush" on C.
> A blocks and intercepts B action.
>
> Can B play "Thoughts Betrayed"?
>
> - Situation 2:
>

Of course not. Blessing of Chaos specifically prohibits the opposing
minion from playing cards with Dominate when in combat with your
minion. Since Thoughts Betrayed is a combat card, the other minion
can't play it.

> A enters combat with B.
> A plays "Burning Wrath" as strike.
> B plays "Entombment" at superior, as strike.
>
> Since A is going to torpor, does B still takes the damage, (and
> goes to torpor too) ?
>

Yes. Both strikes occur at the same time.

-Chris

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Chris Berger wrote:
> Luis P. Duarte wrote:
> > A sucessfully plays "Blessing of Chaos" on him[self].

> > B plays "Bum's Rush" on C.
> > A blocks and intercepts B action.
> >
> > Can B play "Thoughts Betrayed"?
> >

> Of course not. Blessing of Chaos specifically prohibits the opposing
> minion from playing cards with Dominate when in combat with your
> minion. Since Thoughts Betrayed is a combat card, the other minion
> can't play it.

Correct.

Only since TB has been ruled/errata to be played "as combat is entered"
rather than "before combat". Without that errata, the case would be
less clear.

> > A enters combat with B.
> > A plays "Burning Wrath" as strike.
> > B plays "Entombment" at superior, as strike.
> >
> > Since A is going to torpor, does B still takes the damage, (and
> > goes to torpor too) ?
> >
> Yes. Both strikes occur at the same time.

Correct.
